findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex-wide lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the whole build, serializing builds. Now the lock is only taken around the final map write. Two callers that miss the cache for the same NamespacedResource (for example a Search request via getOrCreateIndex racing with a watch event handled by handleEvent, or init racing with either) will both run the full build. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold), bleve.New on the same directory will fail for the second caller, or the two indexes will each be built and one silently overwrites the other in b.cache, leaking an open bleve index. The fix needs per-key singleflight or a check-again under lock before building, not just finer locking around the cache write.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock, while BuildIndex now writes to b.cache under cacheMu. Concurrent map read and write is a data race and can crash the process with 'concurrent map iteration and map write'. TotalDocs is called from searchSupport.init for logging. The read should take cacheMu.RLock().

findings.title: init goroutines write shared variables without synchronization
findings.body: Inside group.Go, the closure does `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)`. Both `totalBatchesIndexed` and the outer `err` are shared across the errgroup goroutines, so this is a data race on each increment and assignment. A failing build can also overwrite another goroutine's error, so group.Wait may return the wrong error. Use a local err variable inside the closure and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Partially initialized resources leak when Init fails in NewResourceServer
findings.body: If s.Init returns an error, NewResourceServer returns nil without calling s.cancel() or Stop. The background context created earlier, and any watcher goroutines already started by initWatcher or search init, are never torn down. Since init now runs at construction time and can fail, the failure path should cancel the context and release lifecycle resources.

findings.title: Index build now blocks construction and can fail server startup without a timeout
findings.body: Moving Init into NewResourceServer means the full index build (search.init, which walks every namespace/resource) now runs synchronously before the server is returned. Callers, including module startup, now block on that work and fail hard if any build errors, where previously the failure only surfaced on individual RPCs. The context passed is the unbounded background context with no deadline. The PR asks whether anything depended on lazy init. Callers that constructed the server and expected it to be cheap or to tolerate index failure are affected, and this needs to be called out and tested.

findings.title: Stop no longer gates RPCs, and initErr is written without synchronization
findings.body: Previously every RPC called s.Init, which returned s.initErr, so calls after Stop returned 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped'. The Init calls were removed from Read, List, Create, Update, Delete, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob and Watch, so those errors are no longer returned after Stop. Stop also writes s.initErr without any lock while other goroutines may read it. Both are behavior changes that the PR does not mention.

findings.title: Postgres variant of the storage-server integration test is now skipped
findings.body: The new skip for postgres means the only test that exercises the storage server target with a real database no longer runs for postgres in CI. The change is unrelated to the PR's stated goals (init, tracing, indexing speed) and reduces coverage of the startup path that this PR changes, with no linked issue tracking the re-enable.
